key_insight: C$^{2}$R improves sparse autoencoder interpretability by enforcing cross-sample consistency so each semantic feature is more likely to map to one unified latent instead of splitting or being absorbed by exceptions.
engineering_relevance: For scalable LLM interpretability systems, this offers a principled regularizer that preserves reconstruction quality while making learned dictionaries more reliable and easier to analyze.
method: Penalize co-activation of directionally similar latents across samples.
Encourage a consistent latent assignment for the same semantic concept within a batch.
Reduce redundant or interfering latents that cause feature splitting and absorption.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comprehensive evaluation showing C$^{2}$R mitigates both splitting and absorption while preserving reconstruction fidelity.
watch_item: The regularizer adds cross-sample coupling, so tuning the similarity threshold and penalty strength will likely be important to avoid suppressing genuinely related features.
paper_title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
